chunks: And everything in it from Jabir ibn Abdullah Al-Ansari, I have narrated it from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah Al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il Al-Barmaki, from Ja'far ibn Ahmad, from Abdullah ibn Al-Fadl, from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Jabir ibn Yazid Al-Ju'fi, from Jabir ibn Abdullah Al-Ansari.

key_terms.الْمُفَضَّلِ بْنِ عُمَرَ: Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, a well-known narrator
key_terms.جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْأَنْصَارِ: Jabir ibn Abdullah Al-Ansari, a prominent companion of the Prophet
key_terms.جَابِرِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ الْجَعْفِيِّ: Jabir ibn Yazid Al-Ju'fi, a major narrator from the Imams
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a honorific for companions or narrators
key_terms.عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُوسَى: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa, a key narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: What is the chain of narrators for Jab ibn Abdullah Al-Ansari in this hadith collection?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq provides a detailed isnad (chain of transmission) to authenticate the narrations of Jabir ibn Abdullah Al-Ansari, tracing the lineage from the companion through prominent Kufan and Ahl al-Bayt scholars to the author himself. This rigorous verification underscores the reliability of the reports in *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, a cornerstone of Shia fiqh, by linking the companion's knowledge to the Imams via trusted intermediaries like Al-Ju'fi and Al-Fadl ibn Dinar.
